chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Musicians debating bebop at Harlem's Rhythm Club
summary: Benny Harris played bop and swing on Horace's one-nighters; musicians argued about bop at Harlem's Rhythm Club like the old Hawkins meetings.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Was there much talk among jazz musicians at that time, you know, pro and con, or did it just --

Oh, yeah. They discussed it. I remember the Rhythm Club down there in Harlem, 132nd and 7th Avenue, musicians used to meet there and discuss all that. This is when Bird upset everybody -- you know this is Charlie Parker, blowing his horn, and the guys, they more or less did like we used to have those meetings up to Coleman Hawkins', you know, except it was more public. And the guys had do's and don'ts about it. A lot of guys would say, well, you better get with it, because this is where it is going to be. This is where it is, man, you know, one of those things. And --
Did musicians, some of them, feel threatened by it, do you think?
